title: Quantum Computing in focus as Titan Partners starts with Buy rating

content:
Quantum Computing QUBT was in focus on Tuesday as investment firm Titan Partners started coverage on the firm with a Buy rating and a $20 price target.

Shares were little changed in premarket trading.

“Headquartered in Hoboken, New Jersey, QCi designs and manufactures room-temperature, low-power photonic quantum systems and controls its stack end to end, from thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) chip fabrication to advanced packaging, components, secure communications, and complete quantum machines,” Titan Partners analyst Scott Buck wrote in a note to clients. “The top line is inflecting, as revenue grew from $61.0K in 2Q25 to $5.6M in 2Q26, the contract backlog stands at $42.5M, and a $1.3B portfolio of cash and investments funds the ramp without further dilution. As Fab 2 qualifies and the backlog converts through 2027, we expect QUBT shares to work toward our $20 target.”

Delving deeper, Buck said that Quantum Computing owns every layer of the quantum stack after the NHanced acquisition, and controls components through the Luminar Semiconductor deal, which gives the company control over cost, capacity and delivery.

“McKinsey estimates quantum technologies could create up to $2.7T of economic value by 2035, with the market for quantum hardware, software, and services reaching $60.0B to $100.0B,” Buck added. “Just four liquid U.S.-listed pure-plays offer exposure: IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave, and QUBT. Among them, QUBT is the only vertically integrated manufacturer and the cheapest credible name at 13.4x 2027E EV/sales.”
